Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract in `README.md`, then inspect the current rollout evidence. I’ll use the required `read-wake-visual-signals-first` and `fish-control-primitives` skills before settling on the single candidate, and I’ll keep all edits inside this Phase 2 workspace.

The workspace requires the inherited guidance plus every sampled solver’s score, observation, metrics, and keyframe evidence. I’m inventorying those now; the visual-first skill will determine which two rendered views must be inspected before any policy edit.

All four sampled runs confirm the required direct-uniform still-water setup and all terminate at the upper virtual boundary. The strongest run is `807c…` (minimum 11.512 L); I’m now reading its top-down and oblique rows against the three weaker failure sheets, as the visual-first skill requires.

The inherited guidance points to a specific missing mechanism: the best posterior-bias controller makes real distance progress but repeatedly crosses the target bearing before its final upper-boundary drift. I’m checking the optimizer provenance logs now so the new lesson and hypothesis reflect what earlier workers actually intended and observed, not just the scalar summaries.

The inherited `be67…` result is an important negative control: adding a speed-gated course cue through half-cycle asymmetry still exited at 8.690 T and only reached 11.967 L, well behind the posterior mean-tail controller’s 11.512 L. I’ll preserve the proven posterior mean-curvature actuator and test the course cue there, which isolates whether the observation is useful without repeating the failed half-cycle translation. I’m recording that diagnosis and the bookshelf transfer block before touching the policy, as required by both skills.

The single solver candidate is now a course-damped posterior mean-curvature controller: it keeps every part of the best sampled carrier/actuator mapping and adds only the new body-frame, forward-speed-gated response residual. Next I’m updating the durable guidance with the inherited `be67…` negative result so later workers do not mistake “course cue present” for an effective controller.

The required notes and durable guidance are both updated. I’m invoking the workspace’s configured check-runner now; it will perform only the guidance-difference, lightweight Julia contract, and edit-boundary checks—no CFD. In parallel I’ll inspect the final diff and reflection behavior locally.

The configured check-runner invocation itself failed before executing because its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable on this account. I’m applying its exact three-command contract directly instead, still without CFD; any failure will be repaired and rerun.

The first check exposed a rendered-workspace metadata defect: `README.md` marks the same parent optimizer twice, so the checker sees two copied parents and cannot compare guidance. I’ll remove only the duplicate marker (leaving the single assigned-parent entry intact), then rerun the check; this does not alter solver or evaluation semantics.

The guidance check now passes. The Julia check is blocked only by the shell environment (`julia: command not found`, plus unrelated login-profile SSH warnings), not by a policy assertion. I’m locating the workspace/runtime Julia binary and will rerun the same contract with login-shell startup disabled.

Implemented exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl) preserves the strongest posterior mean-curvature controller and adds a forward-speed-gated body-frame course-error residual.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md) records the visual diagnosis, hypothesis, falsification criteria, and bookshelf transfer block.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md) now captures the inherited course-aware half-cycle failure as a reusable negative lesson.

Validation:

- Guidance material-change check: PASS
- Solver edit-boundary check: PASS
- Parameter-schema comparison: PASS
- Julia runtime check could not execute because Julia is unavailable in the environment.
- No CFD was run.

I also removed a duplicate assigned-parent marker from `README.md` that initially prevented the required guidance check from running.
